id:
The entry's own number. Leave the number of an existing word as it is.
Press ENTER in this box to fill in the next free number for a new word.
lemma_1:
The headword in dictionary form, then a space and a number, for example kamma 1. Use a two-part number (a 1.1, a 2.1) when the same word comes from different roots.
A headword that is already in the dictionary shows an ERROR.
lemma_2: The clean Pāḷi form without a number. A noun in -a takes its nominative singular: masculine dhamma gives dhammo, neuter citta gives cittaṃ. A prefix ends with a hyphen (saṃ-). A suffix starts with one (-dhā).
pos:
The part of speech. Choose ONE of the listed values.
TYPE to narrow the list.
grammar: Grammatical details such as gender or tense. For a noun made from a participle write pp of, prp of or ptp of plus the source word. For a present tense made from a causative or passive base write caus of or pass of plus the source word.
derived_from: The word this one is made from, or the prefix or prefixes plus root it is made from.
neg: Choose neg if the word is a negative, for example with the prefix na- or a-. Choose neg x2 if it has two negative prefixes.
verb: For causative (caus), passive (pass), denominative (deno), desiderative (desid), intensive (intens) or impersonal (impers) forms. These can be combined, for example impers, pass. For a present tense the other half goes in grammar.
trans: For verbs and verbal participles. trans takes a direct object (+acc). intrans takes none, or takes its object in another case such as +instr. ditrans takes two or more objects.
plus_case: The case in which the object of the verb or verbal participle stands, for example +acc or +dat. Write +inf if the word takes an infinitive.
meaning_1: The English meaning of the word in the context of your example. Put the best-fitting gloss first, then a few synonyms in order of importance, separated by semicolons. Say what the word means here, not everything it can mean.
meaning_lit: The literal meaning of the word, only where it is useful and differs from meaning_1.
meaning_2: A meaning taken from an older dictionary, for example Buddhadatta, when it differs from meaning_1.
root_key: The root this word comes from, with its number. Choose from the roots already in the dictionary, and pick the numbered entry whose meaning fits.
root_sign: The sign that shows the root's group (gaṇa), for example a for group 1 (√bhū) or ya for group 3 (√div). A causative or passive adds signs such as *aya or iya, written together with it.
root_base: The root plus its sign, which gives the base the word is built on. It also shows causative, passive, denominative, future, irregular and desiderative forms.
family_root: The prefix or prefixes plus root that this word belongs to, for example √kaṅkh. All words made from the same prefix and root are grouped under it.
family_word: For a word that does not come from a root: the word it is built on. All words made from the same component word are grouped under it.
family_compound: For a compound: the component words in dictionary form, separated by a space. If a part is not yet in the dictionary, add it as a new word first.
family_idioms: For an idiom: the words it is made of, in dictionary form, separated by a space.
construction: How the word is built, left to right. A root word: na > a + pati + √i + tya. A compound: na + kakkasa. Prefixes, then root or base, then derivative suffixes, then ending. Add a SECOND LINE for a secondary derivative.
derivative: The kind of derivative: kita (primary), kicca (primary, forming potential participles) or taddhita (secondary).
suffix: The last suffix, the one that decides the kind of derivative, for example a.
phonetic:
The sound changes the word has gone through in vowels and consonants, for example thy > cch or ā > a.
The PENCIL button next to this box edits the list of rules.
compound_type:
The type of compound, for example kammadhāraya or chaṭṭhī tappurisa. For a bahubbīhi, write the type it came from first, for example digu > bahubbīhi.
The PENCIL button next to this box edits the list of rules.
compound_construction: The compound written out in full, with the declined ending of each component in BOLD, for example akataṃ + ñū with aṃ in bold.
non_root_in_comps: Mostly unused. Leave it empty unless you know what it is for.
non_ia: If the word comes from a language outside Indo-Aryan, give the source word and the language, for example erukku (Tamil).
sanskrit: The closest Sanskrit word, from Monier-Williams or Edgerton. A prefix and root found there go in square brackets, for example [kṛ].
source_1: Where example 1 comes from, as a DPR quick link: book and number with no space, for example SN11.1.
sutta_1: The name of the sutta that example 1 comes from, usually as in the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana text.
example_1: A clear sentence that shows the headword in context. BOLD the headword in its inflected form. Avoid hyphens in the sentence, except in very long compounds.
translation_1:
An English translation of example 1. It helps you check the example.
It is NOT saved in the dictionary entry.
source_2: Where example 2 comes from, as a DPR quick link: book and number with no space, for example SN11.1.
sutta_2: The name of the sutta that example 2 comes from, usually as in the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana text.
example_2: A second clear sentence that shows the headword in context. BOLD the headword in its inflected form. Avoid hyphens in the sentence, except in very long compounds.
translation_2:
An English translation of example 2. It helps you check the example.
It is NOT saved in the dictionary entry.
antonym: A word with the opposite meaning in this context. Separate several with a comma and a space.
synonym: A word with a similar meaning in this context. Separate several with a comma and a space.
var_phonetic: Other forms of the headword that differ only in sound, found in Pāḷi texts. Separate several with a comma and a space.
var_text: Variant readings of the headword found in other Pāḷi texts. Separate several with a comma and a space.
commentary:
What the Aṭṭhakathā or Ṭīkā says the word means here. BOLD the headword.
The SEARCH TOOLS button opens tools for finding the passage.
notes: Notes and information from other sources that help a reader understand the word.
cognate: English cognates of the headword, if there are any.
link: For plants, animals and historical figures: the Wikipedia link.
family_set:
The thematic sets this word belongs to, for example grammatical terms; prefixes.
TYPE to search the list, then choose one or more.
origin: Where the data of this entry came from, for example pass1 or pass2.
stem:
The part of the word that does not decline, without the ending.
! means no real stem: the word is built entirely from its pattern.
A star (*) means do not list all the forms (an irregular word).
- is for an indeclinable.
pattern: The pattern by which the word declines or conjugates. Choose one from the inflection templates. The stem and the pattern together make all the inflected forms.
comment:
A note to the reviewer about this word, for example why you added or changed it.
Contributors other than the main editor see an ERROR until they write one.
It is kept with your addition or correction, NOT in the dictionary entry.
